@ a maker under .up~(2) gives two events a frame in the order of its runs, and the wrapper gives the same events
@ a wrapper twice wrapped, and a wrapper with .up~(2), gives four events a frame: the tick of the inner is 2 (2 p + i) + j
@ a wrapper under .down~(2) gives its two events at the frames of its ticks, 0 2 4, and none between them
@ a wrapper under when~ gives no events on the frames where it stops, and its sample_tick() goes on (the position of the caller)
process 0 frames=4 in g=[true false true true]
@ a receiver in the body of the maker ticks right after each run: the two elements of a frame are the sums after each of the two events
@ a call under .up~(2) that is reset by its own events: the reset comes after the run that gave the event, before the next run
@ two receivers of one maker: one reset by an event of the maker comes back to 0 before it adds that event, the other sums all
@ a run that gives None gives no event: the first of the two runs (1 3 5 at the frames 0 1 2) or the second (2 4 6)
@ the events of a run of a Bool, an F32 and a struct come in the order of the runs, two a frame
@ a maker under .up~(8) gives eight events a frame: 0 .. 7 in one frame, the frame p has 8 p .. 8 p + 7
@ makers in a block give their events at the position of the tick of the boundary, in the order of the runs
@ the calls of process cut the run anywhere, a call of 0 frames too, and reset starts again: the values of one run
